analysis.title: US EQUITIES - panic / positioning
key_insights: SPX is below 7k and the GS Vol Panic Index finished Friday at 9.8 out of 10. Historically panic readings like this have been a good opportunity to start adding risk.

Two differences versus past episodes: the Fed is hiking rather than cutting, and investor positioning is mixed. In five episodes with panic above 9 during a hiking regime, subsequent three-month returns averaged +0.4%.

Hedge funds have been through a large unwind. GS PB data through Thursday showed a third straight week of global equity selling, short sales outpaced long buying 1.5 to 1, and US single stocks were shorted every day last week, the largest weekly shorting since June 2022.

Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42.3%, the 1st percentile over the past year. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell more than 22 pts since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low. Momentum exposure went from a record +70% in June to negative.
Fundamental L/S managers lost another 1.2% Friday, with US-focused managers down 1.6% (a 2.6 standard deviation move). Fundamental L/S is down 2.1% MTD while systematic L/S is up 1.5%.

Other cohorts remain well invested. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at the 75th percentile, US equity mutual funds and ETFs took in nearly $170bn since the start of Q4, and asset manager equity futures length is at the 82nd percentile.

The desk sees vol panic and HF capitulation but not the broad investor washout that has produced the strongest rebounds. It notes parallels to Q4 2018, when the October 2018 panic was followed by another 6.8% decline over three months.

High-Beta Cyclicals are up 12% YTD while broad US AI is negative YTD. In 4Q-2018 high beta cyclicals fell 23% and lagged SPX by 10pp, and at 15x fwd PE the basket trades at a 40% premium to its 2018 trough multiple, so it could underperform sharply if growth fears replace inflation fears.

GS Research frames a wide SPX range of roughly 5,800 if valuations normalize toward the 30-year average on trend earnings, versus 8,100 if investors regain confidence in consensus earnings and multiples recover.

Three catalysts for a sustainable recovery: greater confidence in AI earnings and monetization, a more dovish Fed, or further positioning reduction. HF reduction has been plentiful, but less so across the broader market.
CTAs are still a source of supply but most of the risk sits outside the US. The model shows CTAs short US equities, and they would be buyers on a bounce.
Technicals are fragile. Dealer gamma is negative entering a holiday-shortened week and S&P futures top-of-book depth is at the lowest since April 2025.

The desk has more conviction in vol. VXN finished Friday at its highest since COVID, VXSMH closed at an all-time high, and the front of the vol curve is sharply inverted. Vol has overshot without needing a call on the equity bottom.

The desk prefers underwriting vol to chasing stocks. Selling puts at levels it would be comfortable adding length, especially in tech where vol repricing is most extreme, is preferred over buying delta. The desk says it is near a tactical entry.

sector_views.rationale: Up 12% YTD at 15x fwd PE, a 40% premium to the 2018 trough multiple, and vulnerable if the Q4 2018 pattern repeats.
Vol repricing is most extreme here, making put selling attractive, but the AI earnings debate is unresolved.

earnings_insights: The AI earnings debate is front and center, particularly 2027/28 AI earnings, capex and monetization. Broad US AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is negative YTD.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Equities have sold off sharply over several weeks.
Extreme panic has historically been a good entry point, but less so under a hiking Fed.
Wide distribution tied to AI earnings confidence and valuation multiples.

trade_ideas.description: Sell puts at levels where the desk would be comfortable adding length, particularly in tech and semis where vol repricing is most extreme
trade_ideas.rationale: Investors are paid considerably more to take equity risk, with the ability to add exposure at lower entry levels if the unwind continues.
trade_ideas.risk: Taking downside risk if this becomes a more sustained selloff.

risk_factors: Hiking Fed, with subsequent three-month returns averaging only +0.4% after panic above 9 in hiking regimes.
Q4 2018 analog: another 6.8% decline followed the October 2018 panic.
Broader investor positioning remains elevated and has not washed out.
Unresolved AI earnings, capex and monetization debate.
Negative dealer gamma and thin S&P futures liquidity.
High-beta cyclicals could underperform if growth uncertainty replaces inflation anxiety.

tension_points.bull_case: Vol panic at 9.8 out of 10 and the HF unwind to five-year low beta-adjusted leverage point to a tactical entry, with CTAs short US equities and buyers on a bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: Broader positioning stays elevated (sentiment 75th percentile, $170bn inflows), the Fed is hiking, and the Q4 2018 analog saw another 6.8% decline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained selloff that continues the unwind, with the Fed not turning dovish and AI earnings confidence not recovering.
